/-!
# Conjecture 10.65

by A. N. Fomin

Determine the structure of infinite 2-transitive permutation groups $(G, \Omega)$ in which
the stabilizer of a point $\alpha \in \Omega$ has the form
$G_{\alpha} = A \cdot G_{\alpha \beta}$, where $G_{\alpha \beta}$ is the stabilizer of two
points $\alpha, \beta$, $\alpha \ne \beta$, such that $G_{\alpha \beta}$ contains an element
inverting the subgroup $A$. Suppose, in particular, that $A \setminus \{1\}$ contains at most
two conjugacy classes of $G_{\alpha}$; does $G$ then possess a normal subgroup isomorphic to
$PSL_2$ over a field?

Only the yes/no question is formalised here. The first part of the problem
("determine the structure") is not a statable proposition.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.65» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G Ω : Type) [Group G] [MulAction G Ω] [FaithfulSMul G Ω] [Infinite Ω]
      [IsMultiplyPretransitive G Ω 2] (α β : Ω) (A : Subgroup (stabilizer G α)),
      α ≠ β →
      (A : Set (stabilizer G α)) * (stabilizer (stabilizer G α) β : Set (stabilizer G α)) =
        Set.univ →
      (∃ g ∈ stabilizer (stabilizer G α) β, ∀ a ∈ A, g * a * g⁻¹ = a⁻¹) →
      (∃ S : Set (ConjClasses (stabilizer G α)), S.encard ≤ 2 ∧
        (A : Set (stabilizer G α)) \ {1} = {a | ConjClasses.mk a ∈ S}) →
      ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (N : Subgroup G), N.Normal ∧ Nonempty (N ≃* PSL(2, F)) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Let $(G, \Omega)$ be an infinite 2-transitive permutation group. Let $\alpha \ne \beta$ be
points of $\Omega$, and suppose that the point stabilizer $G_{\alpha}$ has the form
$G_{\alpha} = A \cdot G_{\alpha \beta}$ for a subgroup $A \le G_{\alpha}$, where
$G_{\alpha \beta}$ is the stabilizer of the two points $\alpha, \beta$ and contains an
element $g$ inverting $A$ (that is, $g a g^{-1} = a^{-1}$ for all $a \in A$). Suppose in
addition that $A \setminus \{1\}$ contains at most two conjugacy classes of $G_{\alpha}$,
that is, $A \setminus \{1\}$ is a union of at most two $G_{\alpha}$-conjugacy classes.
Does $G$ then possess a normal subgroup isomorphic to $PSL_2(F)$ for some field $F$?

Here a permutation group $(G, \Omega)$ is a group $G$ acting faithfully on a set $\Omega$;
it is infinite when $\Omega$ is infinite (for a faithful 2-transitive action this is
equivalent to $G$ being infinite). The product $A \cdot G_{\alpha \beta}$ is the setwise
product $\{a h : a \in A,\ h \in G_{\alpha \beta}\}$, and $G_{\alpha \beta}$ is the
stabilizer of $\beta$ in the group $G_{\alpha}$. "Isomorphic to $PSL_2$ over a field" means
abstractly isomorphic, as a group, to $PSL_2(F) = SL_2(F)/Z(SL_2(F))$ for some field $F$.

claims.decomposer_note: Open-ended classification request ('determine the structure') whose deliverable is a description of the groups; neither the statement nor the background asserts a candidate classification, so there is no Prop to state (the hypotheses — G_α = A·G_{αβ} as a product of subgroups, an element of G_{αβ} inverting every element of A, which forces A abelian — are only reused as context for the second question).

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ such (G,Ω), ∃ field F, ∃ N ≤ G normal with N ≃* PSL₂(F)), quantified over all infinite 2-transitive (G,Ω) with a subgroup A ≤ G_α such that G_α = A·G_{αβ} (setwise product; whether A ∩ G_{αβ} = 1 / A normal in G_α is intended is not stated, though 'A∖{1} is a union of at most two G_α-conjugacy classes' forces A ◁ G_α), some g ∈ G_{αβ} with g a g⁻¹ = a⁻¹ for all a ∈ A, and A∖{1} a union of at most two G_α-conjugacy classes; the field F is unspecified (any field, PSL₂(F) = SL₂(F)/center), and 'isomorphic to PSL₂ over a field' means abstractly isomorphic as a group.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state mutually equivalent, faithful formalizations: faithful action [FaithfulSMul G Ω] (needed, since the conclusion is about normal subgroups of G), Mathlib's IsMultiplyPretransitive G Ω 2 (verified via is_two_pretransitive_iff to be ordinary 2-transitivity; c07 spells it out directly), infinitude on Ω or G (equivalent under faithful + 2-transitive), setwise product G_α = A·G_{αβ} with no unstated A ∩ G_{αβ} = 1 / normality assumption, an element g ∈ G_{αβ} with g a g⁻¹ = a⁻¹ on A, 'A∖{1} is a union of ≤ 2 G_α-conjugacy classes' (all encodings use encard / Finite ∧ ncard / Finset / Fin n so an infinite family of classes is excluded), and the conclusion ∃ field F, ∃ normal N ≤ G with N ≃* PSL(2, F) (= SL₂(F)/Z(SL₂(F)) in Mathlib). c01 was chosen as the most literal: A is a subgroup of the group G_α, G_{αβ} is the stabilizer of β inside G_α (checked: membership ↔ g • β = β), and 'conjugacy classes of G_α' is literally ConjClasses (stabilizer G α). I verified in a scratch file that its class-union encoding forces A ◁ G_α, as the decomposition notes predict. Shipped with c01's declaration unchanged and a slightly tightened docstring; compiles with only the sorry warning.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's reading of \"A ∖ {1} contains at most two conjugacy classes of G_α\" as \"A ∖ {1} is a union of at most two G_α-conjugacy classes\" is the standard group-theoretic idiom and is what I formalised; I confirmed in a scratch lemma that it forces A ◁ G_α as the notes claim. The alternative literal reading (\"the number of full G_α-classes contained in A ∖ {1} is ≤ 2\") would make the hypothesis vacuous for non-normal A and is clearly not intended. Dropping the \"determine the structure\" part is correct since it has no statable Prop.

open MulAction
open scoped MatrixGroups Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«10.65»

/--
Let $(G, \Omega)$ be an infinite 2-transitive permutation group. Let $\alpha \ne \beta$ be
points of $\Omega$, and suppose that the point stabilizer $G_{\alpha}$ has the form
$G_{\alpha} = A \cdot G_{\alpha \beta}$ for a subgroup $A \le G_{\alpha}$, where
$G_{\alpha \beta}$ is the stabilizer of the two points $\alpha, \beta$ and contains an
element $g$ inverting $A$ (that is, $g a g^{-1} = a^{-1}$ for all $a \in A$). Suppose in
addition that $A \setminus \{1\}$ contains at most two conjugacy classes of $G_{\alpha}$,
that is, $A \setminus \{1\}$ is a union of at most two $G_{\alpha}$-conjugacy classes.
Does $G$ then possess a normal subgroup isomorphic to $PSL_2(F)$ for some field $F$?

Here a permutation group $(G, \Omega)$ is a group $G$ acting faithfully on a set $\Omega$;
it is infinite when $\Omega$ is infinite (for a faithful 2-transitive action this is
equivalent to $G$ being infinite). The product $A \cdot G_{\alpha \beta}$ is the setwise
product $\{a h : a \in A,\ h \in G_{\alpha \beta}\}$, and $G_{\alpha \beta}$ is the
stabilizer of $\beta$ in the group $G_{\alpha}$. "Isomorphic to $PSL_2$ over a field" means

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.65» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G Ω : Type) [Group G] [MulAction G Ω] [FaithfulSMul G Ω] [Infinite Ω]
      [IsMultiplyPretransitive G Ω 2] (α β : Ω) (A : Subgroup (stabilizer G α)),
      α ≠ β →
      (A : Set (stabilizer G α)) * (stabilizer (stabilizer G α) β : Set (stabilizer G α)) =
        Set.univ →
      (∃ g ∈ stabilizer (stabilizer G α) β, ∀ a ∈ A, g * a * g⁻¹ = a⁻¹) →
      (∃ S : Set (ConjClasses (stabilizer G α)), S.encard ≤ 2 ∧
        (A : Set (stabilizer G α)) \ {1} = {a | ConjClasses.mk a ∈ S}) →
      ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (N : Subgroup G), N.Normal ∧ Nonempty (N ≃* PSL(2, F)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.65»

items: "Permutation group (G, Ω)" is modelled as a faithful group action: [MulAction G Ω] [FaithfulSMul G Ω]. Faithfulness matters for the conclusion (a non-faithful action would add a kernel as a normal subgroup), so it is included.

"Infinite" is taken as Infinite Ω. For a faithful 2-transitive action this is equivalent to Infinite G (faithful ⇒ finite Ω gives finite G; 2-transitive on infinite Ω ⇒ G infinite), and Infinite Ω is the more robust choice.
2-transitivity is Mathlib's MulAction.IsMultiplyPretransitive G Ω 2 (transitivity on ordered pairs of distinct points), the standard notion.

The point stabilizer G_α is MulAction.stabilizer G α, and everything about A and G_{αβ} is stated inside the group G_α: A : Subgroup (stabilizer G α) and G_{αβ} := stabilizer (stabilizer G α) β (the stabilizer of β in the group G_α, i.e. G_α ∩ G_β). This makes "conjugacy classes of G_α" literally ConjClasses (stabilizer G α).

G_α = A · G_{αβ} is the setwise product (A : Set _) * (G_{αβ} : Set _) = Set.univ in the group G_α. No extra assumption such as A ∩ G_{αβ} = 1 or A ◁ G_α is added, since the source does not state them (normality follows from the conjugacy-class hypothesis anyway; verified in a scratch lemma).
"G_{αβ} contains an element inverting the subgroup A" is ∃ g ∈ G_{αβ}, ∀ a ∈ A, g * a * g⁻¹ = a⁻¹.

"A ∖ {1} contains at most two conjugacy classes of G_α" is read, following the decomposition table, as: A ∖ {1} is a union of at most two G_α-conjugacy classes, formalised as ∃ S : Set (ConjClasses (stabilizer G α)), S.encard ≤ 2 ∧ (A : Set _) \ {1} = {a | ConjClasses.mk a ∈ S}. encard (ℕ∞-valued) is used instead of ncard so that an infinite S is not accepted. The degenerate case S = ∅ (A trivial) is allowed literally by "at most two" but cannot occur with the other hypotheses (G_α = G_{αβ} would force |Ω| = 2).

"A normal subgroup isomorphic to PSL₂ over a field" is ∃ (F : Type) (_ : Field F) (N : Subgroup G), N.Normal ∧ Nonempty (N ≃* PSL(2, F)), with PSL(2, F) = Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) F = SL₂(F)/Z(SL₂(F)) from Mathlib; abstract group isomorphism. The field is arbitrary (finite fields cannot actually occur since a nontrivial normal subgroup of an infinite primitive group is infinite). Restricting F to Type (rather than Type*) loses nothing: G : Type and F embeds into PSL(2, F) ≅ N, so F is small.
α, β and A are universally quantified as hypotheses (rather than existentially inside the antecedent); this is logically equivalent, and by 2-transitivity all pairs (α, β) are conjugate anyway.
All types G, Ω, F are in Type, matching the convention of the existing Kourovka files (e.g. 1_40.lean).

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity in the source: 'A∖{1} contains at most two conjugacy classes of G_α' was read (per the decomposition table and every candidate) as 'A∖{1} is a union of at most two G_α-conjugacy classes'. The weaker reading ('the nontrivial elements of A meet at most two G_α-classes', not forcing A ◁ G_α) was rejected: c02 gives a convincing trivial counterexample under it (G = Sym(Ω) countable, A a regular elementary abelian 2-group on Ω∖{α}), and the stronger reading matches the PSL₂ model (A = unipotent radical of the Borel), so it is the only reading that leaves a meaningful open question. Other choices: 'infinite' is placed on Ω (c01/c03/c05–c08) rather than G (c02/c04); these are equivalent given faithfulness and 2-transitivity. F ranges over Type, which loses nothing since F embeds into N ≤ G : Type. The 'determine the structure' part was dropped as instructed (no statable Prop); no candidate objected to the decomposition. The docstring's explanatory paragraph documents the modeling of 'permutation group', the setwise product and the notion of isomorphism; it contains no review notes or proof sketches.
